title: English File Upper-Intermediate, File 1: questions, helper verbs, the more ... the better (check against the book)

fixIt.text: Who you usually sit next to in class?
fixIt.explain: Present simple questions need do: Who do you usually sit next to?

fixIt.text: Can you tell me where the nearest pharmacy are?
fixIt.explain: One pharmacy: is. Indirect questions keep normal word order.

fixIt.text: How long did it took to get there?
fixIt.explain: After did, use the base form: did it take?

fixIt.text: She hasn't been to Japan, but her brother does.
fixIt.explain: Repeat the helper verb of the first part: hasn't … has.

fixIt.text: I can't swim, but my sister does.
fixIt.explain: can't … can: the same helper verb.

fixIt.text: The more I read, the much I understand.
fixIt.explain: the more …, the more …: two comparatives.

fixIt.text: The sooner we leave, the best.
The older I get, the happiest I am.
I've never been to Laos. Neither am I.
fixIt.explain: Same helper verb as the first sentence (have): Neither have I.

builder.text: Do you know where the station is?
I haven't seen it. Neither have I.

radio.title: My first week at work
radio.text: Starting a new job is never easy. On my first day, everyone asked me questions: where I had studied, how long I had lived in the city, and whether I could speak Chinese. I can't, but my new manager can, so she offered to teach me a few words. The more people I met, the more relaxed I felt. By Friday I knew most of my colleagues' names, and they knew mine. The sooner you learn names, the better.
